description: I1: Attempt attacker-signed SAMLResponse against a SAML connector configured with CA-based signature validation; forged assertion should be rejected (tests cert substitution / trust anchor enforcement).
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must validate SAML signatures against the configured CA trust anchor; an attacker-signed assertion must not be accepted when signature validation is enabled.

oracle_checks.violation_description: SP accepted attacker-signed SAML assertion even though CA-based signature validation was configured (trust anchor substitution / signature validation bypass).
SP-initiated flow did not start; SAML callback result is inconclusive because InResponseTo/relay context may be missing.

description: I1: With ssoIssuer pinned, send a forged SAML assertion with wrong Issuer; should be rejected (tests issuer mismatch enforcement). Includes a control login with correct issuer first.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must bind verification to the configured IdP issuer (ssoIssuer); a SAML assertion with an untrusted Issuer must not be accepted even if otherwise well-formed.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login failed; issuer-mismatch result is inconclusive due to possible connector misconfiguration or missing SP-initiated context.
SP accepted SAML assertion with Issuer not matching pinned ssoIssuer (issuer validation bypass / proof integrity failure).

description: I1: Demonstrate configuration-dependent proof integrity by toggling insecure_skip_signature_validation. First, attacker-signed assertion should be rejected with CA validation; then enable insecure skip and show attacker-signed assertion is accepted (by design) to detect accidental insecure defaults/regressions.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: When signature validation is enabled, Dex must reject attacker-signed SAML assertions; acceptance should only occur when explicitly configured to skip signature validation (guard against insecure default/regression).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Secure (CA-validated) SAML connector accepted attacker-signed assertion; signature verification may be bypassed or trust anchor may be taken from the response.
In insecureSkipSignatureValidation mode, attacker-signed assertion was not accepted; indicates test harness mismatch (not an I1 finding) or connector not actually using insecure mode.

description: Test whether Dex accepts an attacker-signed SAML assertion with the entire <Conditions> element omitted (proof semantics changed after verification). Includes a control login with normal Conditions first.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: If Dex verifies signature but does not enforce semantic constraints in Conditions, it may accept a proof whose consumed semantics omit time/audience restrictions.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login failed; cannot interpret missing-Conditions result as an integrity issue.
Dex accepted an attacker-signed SAML assertion with Conditions omitted (semantic proof changed after verification).

description: I1 proof-integrity check under intentionally insecure SAML connector config: if insecure_skip_signature_validation=true, attacker-signed SAMLResponse may be accepted. This sequence verifies acceptance occurs only under the insecure policy and that the consumed identity matches the forged NameID.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: If signature validation is disabled (insecure_skip_signature_validation=true), Dex may accept attacker-signed SAML assertions; the test ensures this acceptance is configuration-dependent and that the consumed identity corresponds to the forged proof content (NameID/email).

oracle_checks.violation_description: If this assertion fails, the insecure-skip path did not accept attacker-signed SAMLResponse (unexpected for this configuration-dependent test).
Different forged NameID values collapsed into the same downstream subject, indicating proof/identity confusion during consumption.

description: I1/I3-adjacent proof-integrity splice attempt: start two SP-initiated SAML flows (victim then attacker) and try to post an attacker-forged SAMLResponse while reusing the victim RelayState/context. If Dex accepts, it indicates the consumed assertion is not bound to the verified AuthnRequest context (InResponseTo/RelayState binding failure), violating proof integrity.
invariant_hypothesis: I1: Dex must verify the SAMLResponse against the exact SP-initiated request context (RelayState/InResponseTo) it will consume. A forged response must not be accepted when spliced into a different session's RelayState.

oracle_checks.assertion: victim_start_http_status >= 200 AND victim_start_http_status < 400 AND attacker_start_http_status >= 200 AND attacker_start_http_status < 400
oracle_checks.violation_description: Precondition failed: SP-initiated flows did not start successfully; splice test is inconclusive.
Dex accepted a SAMLResponse spliced into a different session's RelayState/InResponseTo context; proof consumed was not bound to the verified request context (proof integrity failure).
Even though the splice should be rejected, Dex appears to have established a session/identity, suggesting it consumed an unbound proof.

description: SAML OneTimeUse replay: perform a control SAML login with <OneTimeUse/>, then replay the exact same assertion (same Assertion/@ID) in a second login. Second attempt must be rejected if OneTimeUse and replay cache are enforced.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: A SAML assertion marked OneTimeUse (and/or with the same Assertion ID) must not be accepted more than once; replaying the same assertion should be rejected.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login with OneTimeUse did not succeed; cannot evaluate replay enforcement.
Dex accepted a replayed SAML assertion marked OneTimeUse (replay should be rejected).

description: Replay a previously accepted SAML assertion after revoking the session from the first login. Revocation should not disable SAML replay protection; the same assertion must still be rejected on reuse.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: SAML assertion replay protection must be independent of downstream session revocation; revoking a session must not allow reusing the same SAML assertion again.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login did not succeed; cannot evaluate replay-after-revocation behavior.
Dex accepted a replayed SAML assertion after session revocation; replay protection may be incorrectly tied to session state.

description: SAML assertion replay without <OneTimeUse/>: reuse the exact same Assertion/@ID and assertion material twice; second attempt must be rejected by replay cache even if OneTimeUse is absent.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Dex must reject a replayed SAML assertion (same Assertion/@ID) even when <OneTimeUse/> is not present; otherwise assertion replay is possible within validity window.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login failed; cannot evaluate replay behavior
Dex accepted replayed SAML assertion with identical Assertion/@ID (replay cache not enforced)

description: Replay persistence across connector reconfiguration: accept a SAML assertion once, delete and recreate the connector, then replay the exact same assertion ID. Replay cache should not be reset by connector lifecycle changes.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Dex replay protection should be durable enough that deleting/recreating the SAML connector does not allow reuse of a previously accepted assertion (same Assertion/@ID).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Seed login failed; cannot evaluate replay after connector recreation
Dex accepted replayed SAML assertion after connector delete/recreate (replay cache reset enables reuse)

description: Test whether Dex incorrectly accepts an expired SAML assertion and/or allows replay of the exact same expired assertion ID across two SP-initiated flows (anti-replay + expiry enforcement). Includes a control valid login first to prove the connector/flow is correctly configured.
invariant_hypothesis: I2: Dex must reject expired SAML assertions (NotOnOrAfter in the past) and must not accept the same Assertion/@ID more than once, even if the assertion is expired.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login did not succeed; cannot attribute later failures/successes to expiry/replay enforcement.
Dex accepted an expired SAML assertion (NotOnOrAfter in the past); expiry enforcement missing.
Dex accepted replay of the same expired SAML Assertion/@ID across two flows; replay protection missing or not keyed correctly.

description: I3 cross-session splicing: start two SP-initiated SAML flows, then swap RelayState between them when posting the SAMLResponse to test whether Dex binds the callback to the correct pending auth request/session.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Dex must reject a SAMLResponse whose RelayState/state belongs to a different SP-initiated flow (no cross-session splicing).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAMLResponse posted with a RelayState/state from a different SP-initiated flow (cross-session splicing).

description: I3 connector binding: initiate an auth flow for one connector_id but post the SAMLResponse to a different connector callback path to test whether Dex enforces connector/session coherence.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Dex must reject SAML callback posts that do not correspond to the connector used to initiate the SP-initiated flow (no step splicing across connectors).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Dex accepted a SAMLResponse on a different connector callback than the one used to initiate the flow (connector/session splicing).

description: I3 coherence across config change: perform a baseline SAML login with insecure signature validation enabled, then tighten connector config to require signature validation and re-attempt attacker-signed SAML login; must be rejected (no stale acceptance path).
invariant_hypothesis: I3: After connector trust policy is tightened, subsequent logins must follow the updated FSM/policy immediately; attacker-signed assertions must not continue to be accepted due to stale state/caching.

oracle_checks.violation_description: After tightening SAML signature validation, Dex still accepted attacker-signed assertions (policy change did not take effect coherently).

description: I3 attack: attempt to reuse the same SP-initiated SAML flow context (RelayState) for a second SAMLResponse (step re-use / callback re-entry). Dex should treat the flow as one-shot and reject the second callback even if it is a fresh assertion.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: The SAML callback must be bound to a single pending auth transaction; reusing the same RelayState/state context for a second SAMLResponse must be rejected (no step re-entry).

description: I3 attack: start two SP-initiated auth flows for two different OIDC clients, then attempt to complete the SAML callback for the second flow but exchange the code using the first client credentials (cross-client splicing).
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization code issuance and redemption must be bound to the initiating client; a code from client-B must not be redeemable by client-A.

description: I3 attack: initiate SP flow, then tamper RelayState on callback (inject different relay_state) to test whether Dex binds the SAMLResponse to the exact issued state/relay context and rejects mismatched relay_state.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: The SAMLResponse must be bound to the exact pending auth request context; tampering RelayState should not allow completing the flow or switching the target session.

description: I3 cross-session splicing attempt by completing flow-A using flow-B's SAMLResponse (InResponseTo mismatch) while keeping flow-A RelayState. Dex should reject because SAMLResponse must match the exact pending AuthnRequest for that RelayState/session.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Dex must bind the SAMLResponse (InResponseTo) to the exact SP-initiated AuthnRequest associated with the pending RelayState/session; cross-flow splicing must be rejected.

description: I3 step-skipping attempt: post a forged SAMLResponse to the connector callback without any prior start_oidc_auth SP-initiated flow. Dex should reject unsolicited/IdP-initiated responses.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Dex must enforce the protocol FSM: SAML callback completion must only be accepted after a matching SP-initiated flow; step skipping must be rejected.

description: I3 cross-session splicing: initiate two parallel SP-initiated SAML auth flows for the same OIDC client, complete both, then attempt to exchange flow-A's authorization code using flow-B's redirect_uri (code/redirect_uri binding confusion). Secure behavior: token exchange must reject mismatched redirect_uri for the code.
invariant_hypothesis: I3: Authorization codes must be bound to the exact initiating request context (including redirect_uri) and not be exchangeable across parallel sessions/flows by swapping redirect_uri parameters.

oracle_checks.assertion: user_flowA_start_http_status >= 200 AND user_flowA_start_http_status < 400 AND user_flowB_start_http_status >= 200 AND user_flowB_start_http_status < 400
oracle_checks.violation_description: Precondition failed: could not initiate both SP-initiated flows; cannot evaluate cross-flow code/redirect_uri binding.

oracle_checks.assertion: user_flowA_login_status >= 200 AND user_flowA_login_status < 400 AND user_flowB_login_status >= 200 AND user_flowB_login_status < 400
oracle_checks.violation_description: Precondition failed: could not complete both SAML callbacks; cannot evaluate code swap behavior.
Dex accepted exchanging flow-A authorization code using flow-B redirect_uri (cross-session splicing / redirect_uri binding failure).
Despite expected rejection of mismatched redirect_uri, a usable session appears to have been created (flow coherence failure).

description: I4 attack: attempt account takeover by asserting victim email while using attacker NameID; verify Dex binds principal to NameID (should not collapse to victim).
invariant_hypothesis: I4: If Dex incorrectly binds downstream subject by emailAttr instead of SAML NameID, an attacker can log in with NameID=attacker but email=victim@example.com and be mapped to the victim's downstream identity.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Attacker NameID mapped to victim identity due to email-based linking (principal binding failure)

description: I4 empty_sub/empty NameID collision: attempt two distinct upstream principals where one uses an empty SAML NameID and another uses a normal NameID; ensure Dex does not map both to the same downstream subject.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: If Dex treats empty/blank SAML NameID as a default or null principal key, distinct upstream principals could collapse into the same downstream identity.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Empty/blank NameID collapsed into another user's downstream identity (principal binding failure)

description: I4 cross_mount_collision analogue for SAML: same NameID authenticating via two different SAML connectors (different IdP issuer) should not collapse if Dex fails to namespace identities by connector/issuer.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: If Dex keys users only by NameID and ignores connector/issuer context, the same NameID from different upstream IdPs could map to the same downstream subject (cross-IdP account collision).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Same NameID from different SAML connectors/issuers collapsed into one downstream identity (cross-IdP principal binding failure)

description: I4 principal-binding attack with config change + re-auth: switch SAML NameID format policy and test whether identities from different NameID formats collapse unexpectedly (persistent vs emailAddress).
invariant_hypothesis: I4: Changing NameIDPolicyFormat (persistent vs emailAddress) should not cause two security-distinct upstream principals to map to the same downstream subject; identities should remain correctly bound to the actual NameID value/format.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Dex merged two security-distinct upstream principals across NameID format policy change (persistent vs emailAddress), collapsing identities unexpectedly
One or both logins failed; identity-collision result is inconclusive for principal-binding

description: Test whether Dex incorrectly canonicalizes SAML NameID values that look numeric, collapsing distinct principals 'user-01' and 'user-1' (leading-zero normalization) into the same downstream subject.
invariant_hypothesis: I4: If Dex normalizes NameID by stripping leading zeros or parsing numeric-like identifiers, two security-distinct upstream principals (NameID='user-01' vs NameID='user-1') could map to the same downstream identity_id.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Baseline failed: mechanism cannot distinguish principals
Principal binding violated: Dex collapsed distinct SAML NameID values differing by leading zeros ('user-01' vs 'user-1') into the same downstream subject
Inconclusive: one or both SAML logins failed (cannot evaluate principal-binding collision if authentication did not complete)

description: I5: Attempt to obtain an authenticated session from a SAML assertion with the entire <Conditions> element removed (no audience/time bounds). Control login uses a normal assertion. If Dex accepts the no-Conditions assertion, it may be granting permissions without upstream intent constraints.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: Dex must not accept SAML assertions lacking Conditions (no AudienceRestriction / time bounds), because that would allow permissions beyond UpstreamIntent(auth_context) ∩ BrokerPolicy(config).

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control SAML login failed; cannot attribute subsequent acceptance/rejection to Conditions enforcement.
Dex accepted a SAML assertion with no <Conditions>, enabling permissions without upstream audience/time intent.

description: I5: Configure SAML connector to gate authentication on membership in an allowed group and filter emitted groups. Then attempt to authenticate as a user with no allowed group but with other groups, to see if Dex mistakenly grants a session/policies anyway (authz binding failure). Includes re-auth after config change.
invariant_hypothesis: I5: When allowedGroups is configured, Dex must not grant an authenticated session (and thus any effective permissions) unless the upstream assertion includes at least one allowed group; filterGroups must not weaken gating.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control login with allowed group failed; cannot evaluate allowedGroups gating.
Dex granted a session to a user lacking any allowedGroups membership, violating authorization binding (permissions granted without upstream group intent).

description: I5 attack: attempt to bypass group-based authorization binding by confusing Dex's SAML groups parsing. Configure connector to require allowedGroups=['admins'] and set a nonstandard groups_delim. Then authenticate an attacker whose assertion carries a single groups attribute value that could be mis-parsed into including 'admins' (e.g., 'devs;admins') even though upstream intent is not true membership. Secure behavior: login rejected (or at least no 'admins' group emitted).
invariant_hypothesis: I5: If Dex mis-parses the SAML groups attribute using an incorrect delimiter, it may treat a single composite group string as containing an allowed group and grant a session/policies beyond upstream intent.

oracle_checks.violation_description: Control admin SAML login failed; cannot evaluate group parsing/authorization binding.

Dex accepted a SAML login where the only asserted group value was a composite string ('devs;admins'); this suggests group parsing confusion bypassed allowedGroups gating, granting authorization beyond upstream intent.
